The current zproxy-k3s manifest (after PR #59) contains two nearly identical Deployments that differ only in:

title: fix: Docker credentials permission denied on arc-runner-set-org (DOCKER_CONFIG)
body:
## Problem

Runner container działa jako user `runner`, ale Kubernetes montując `buildx-config` (emptyDir) pod `/home/runner/.docker/buildx` tworzy katalog `/home/runner/.docker` z ownerem `root:root`. Efekt: każdy job używający `docker/login-action` kończy się błędem:

```
error saving credentials: open /home/runner/.docker/config.json<random_id>: permission denied
```

## Root cause

W `apps/arc-runner-set-org/values.yaml`:
- `buildx-config` (emptyDir) jest zamontowany pod `/home/runner/.docker/buildx` w kontenerze `runner`
- K8s tworzy mountpoint tworząc katalog rodzica `/home/runner/.docker` jako `root:root`
- `runner` user nie ma write access do `/home/runner/.docker/config.json`

## Fix

Dodać env var `DOCKER_CONFIG=/home/runner/_work/.docker` na kontenerze `runner`. Volume `work` jest emptyDir writable przez usera `runner`.

title: fix: apt-cache nginx upstream for deb.debian.org/debian-security returns 404
body:
## Problem

`apt-get update` w kontenerach Debian Bookworm fails z:
```
E: The repository 'http://deb.debian.org/debian-security bookworm-security Release' does not have a Release file.
```

## Root cause

nginx upstream map kieruje `deb.debian.org` → `ftp.task.gda.pl` (mirror GDA). Mirror GDA **nie hostuje `/debian-security/`** — tylko `/debian/`. Żaden polski mirror Debiana nie replikuje archiwum security.

Debian Bookworm używa `deb.debian.org/debian-security` (nie starego `security.debian.org`), więc oba wpisy w mapie kierują security traffic na zły upstream.

## Fix

Zmiana upstream dla `deb.debian.org` i `security.debian.org` na `deb.debian.org` (Fastly CDN), który hostuje zarówno `/debian/` jak i `/debian-security/`.

title: consolidated: harden orphan-cleaner sidecar securityContext and resources
body:
_Supersedes #108 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Harden the `orphan-cleaner` busybox sidecar in the registry-cache-gcr manifests by:
1. Adding a minimal hardened `securityContext` (no privilege escalation, read-only rootfs, drop all capabilities)
2. Adding resource requests/limits to reduce scheduling uncertainty and blast radius
3. Fixing the cleanup loop startup order to scan immediately before sleeping (resolves orphan link failures during rollout)

## Why

PR #104 review feedback identified two medium-severity issues in `apps/registry-cache-gcr/manifests/zone-ldc.yaml`:

1. **Cleanup loop startup delay:** The cleanup loop sleeps for 1h before the first scan, causing existing orphan links to trigger `short read` failures for up to an hour after rollout. Running one scan immediately and then sleeping at the end of the loop prevents this.

2. **Missing security hardening:** The new sidecar lacks `securityContext` and resource requests/limits, increasing blast radius and scheduling uncertainty. A minimal hardened `securityContext` (allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]) with small resource requests/limits (cpu: 10m/100m, memory: 16Mi/64Mi) reduces risk.

Per @katarzynacc: PR #105 already resolved the cleanup loop startup order. PR #111 implements the remaining security hardening across all three registry-cache-gcr manifests (vrtx, ldc, azpl) and is passing CI (CodeRabbit ✅), awaiting required reviewer approval per branch protection policy.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: apps/registry-cache-gcr/manifests/zone-ldc.yaml` — Add hardened securityContext and resource requests/limits to orphan-cleaner sidecar
- `EDIT: apps/registry-cache-gcr/manifests/zone-azpl.yaml` — Add hardened securityContext and resource requests/limits to orphan-cleaner sidecar
- `EDIT: apps/registry-cache-gcr/manifests/registry-cache-gcr.yaml` — Add hardened securityContext and resource requests/limits to orphan-cleaner sidecar

### Implementation Steps

For each manifest file, locate the `orphan-cleaner` busybox sidecar container and add the following:

1. Add `securityContext` block:
```yaml
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  capabilities:
    drop:
      - ALL
```

2. Add `resources` block:
```yaml
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 10m
    memory: 16Mi
  limits:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 64Mi
```

grep -A 5 "securityContext:" apps/registry-cache-gcr/manifests/registry-cache-gcr.yaml | grep -q "allowPrivilegeEscalation: false"

title: zproxy-k3s-1 CrashLoopBackOff: emptyDir shadows image-provided ssl/ssl_ca dirs, exposed by upstream zabbix-docker entrypoint change
body:
## Summary

`zproxy-k3s-1` is in `CrashLoopBackOff` (469+ restarts over 39h). `zproxy-k3s-0` is healthy. Both deployments are supposedly identical except `ZBX_HOSTNAME`/`Hostname`, but ended up running **different image digests** under the same floating tag `zabbix/zabbix-proxy-sqlite3:7.0-alpine-latest`:

- `zproxy-k3s-0` (healthy, worker6): `sha256:15f97c118500bde61a63cf56b498218a3128dac4a6b6a93336e5ff50c334155c`
- `zproxy-k3s-1` (crashing, worker5): `sha256:af920211d4a57ea2e04e867eabd8899cbc7b3c641b86fb84fcd458207c3c50cd`

## Root cause

1. Both deployments mount the **entire `/var/lib/zabbix` as a single `emptyDir`** volume. This shadows every subdirectory the Zabbix image itself creates at build time under that path (`ssl/certs`, `ssl/keys`, `ssl/ssl_ca`, `ssl/ssl_ca_internal`, ...).
2. The `init-data` init container only recreates two of them: `mkdir -p /var/lib/zabbix/db_data /var/lib/zabbix/snmptraps`. It does **not** recreate the `ssl/*` subdirectories.
3. Upstream `zabbix/zabbix-docker` commit [`5042789a`](https://github.com/zabbix/zabbix-docker/commit/5042789a80c86e7cb1d32630e531cd2c3edf4c61) (2026-09-15, "Fixed OpenSSL rehash function") changed the proxy/server entrypoint:
   - `SSLCALocation` now points at `ssl/ssl_ca_internal` (was `ssl/ssl_ca`).
   - New `openssl_prepare_ca(source_dir, target_dir)` does `rm -rf "$target_dir"/*; cp -a "$source_dir/." "$target_dir/"` with **no existence check** on either directory.
   - `openssl_rehash()` lost its previous `[ -d "$ssl_location" ]` guard.
   - The official reference `compose_zabbix_components.yaml` was updated to mount `ssl_ca` read-only and add a dedicated `tmpfs` for `ssl_ca_internal` — i.e. upstream's own reference deployment mounts these paths **individually**, not as part of one blob volume.
4. `worker6` still has the pre-09-15 digest cached (`imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`), so `zproxy-k3s-0` never hit the new code path. `worker5` pulled the newer digest when the pod was last (re)scheduled there, so `zproxy-k3s-1` hits `cp: can't stat '/var/lib/zabbix/ssl/ssl_ca/.': No such file or directory` on every single boot and never gets past entrypoint init.

Confirmed empirically:
- `kubectl -n monitoring exec <healthy pod> -- ls /var/lib/zabbix/ssl/` → does not exist (image's own built-in dirs are gone, shadowed by the `emptyDir`).
- Diffed the entrypoint `openssl.sh`/`proxy-config.sh` between both actual running image digests (via a throwaway debug pod pinned to the crashing digest) — confirmed the `openssl_prepare_ca` function and missing guard only exist in the newer digest.
- No Zabbix "Web scenario" (HTTP/HTTPS check) exists in this instance (`httptest.get` → `[]`), so `ssl_ca`/`ssl_ca_internal` (custom CA for web-monitoring SSL verification) is **not actually used** — this is dead functionality for us, just needs to not crash the boot.

## Fix

In `apps/zproxy-k3s/manifests/zproxy-k3s.yaml`, for both `zproxy-k3s-0` and `zproxy-k3s-1`:

1. Pin the image to a specific tag/digest instead of the floating `7.0-alpine-latest`, so both replicas always run the identical, tested build and a registry-side update can't silently change behavior again.
2. Extend the `init-data` init container's `mkdir -p` list to also create `ssl/certs`, `ssl/keys`, `ssl/ssl_ca`, `ssl/ssl_ca_internal` (matching what the image itself provides at build time, before the `emptyDir` mount shadows it) — this is cheap, defensive, and makes the deployment resilient to future upstream entrypoint changes regardless of the pin.

## Impact

Zabbix alert `Proxy group [K3S-ProxyGroup]: Availability too low` (currently at 50%) traces back to this. Not a config/VM-level issue — pure container image/manifest mismatch, no production monitoring data is actually lost (the healthy replica keeps the proxy group above 0%), but redundancy is gone while `-1` is down.
